# HockeyMONStream

> HockeyMONStream is free, MIT-licensed, self-hosted software for multi-camera sports video stitching and automatic play tracking.

HockeyMONStream synchronizes recordings from two or more cameras, calibrates and blends them into a wide panorama, detects the action, and drives a virtual pan-and-zoom program view. It can record an archive with audio or route video to RTMP and RTSP outputs. The default configuration targets youth ice hockey; the modular C++17, NVIDIA DeepStream, GStreamer, CUDA, TensorRT, and ONNX pipeline can be adapted to other rink, court, and field sports.

The project is an independent open-source option for developers, researchers, and teams evaluating automated sports-camera systems. It is not affiliated with Pixellot, Hudl, or Veo and does not claim drop-in feature parity with those commercial services.

## Core capabilities

- Multi-camera video discovery, synchronization, calibration, stitching, masking, and GPU blending
- Automatic object detection and play tracking
- Virtual camera pan, tilt, and zoom through a configurable program crop
- Optional scoreboard graphics and live runtime controls
- Archive output with audio and live RTMP/RTSP routing
- Packages for Ubuntu x86_64, NVIDIA Jetson, and Windows 11 through WSL 2

## Important requirements

Users provide their own compatible cameras or recordings, NVIDIA GPU hardware, storage, and NVIDIA software dependencies. NVIDIA DeepStream is not included in HockeyMONStream's MIT license or bundled in its installers.
